text.headline: Timeline of Costa Rica
text.text: Major events in the history of Costa Rica.

events.headline: Earliest Settlements
events.text: The earliest known human settlements in Costa Rica date back to around 500 BC, with indigenous groups such as the Chorotega and Bribri establishing communities.

events.headline: Christopher Columbus Arrives
events.text: Christopher Columbus arrived on the Caribbean coast of Costa Rica during his fourth voyage to the New World, marking the beginning of European interest in the region.

events.headline: Foundation of Cartago
events.text: Cartago was founded as the first permanent Spanish settlement in Costa Rica, serving as the colonial capital and a center for agriculture and trade.

events.headline: Independence from Spain
events.text: Costa Rica, along with other Central American provinces, declared independence from Spanish rule, marking a significant turning point in its history.

events.headline: Costa Rica Becomes a Sovereign State
events.text: Costa Rica officially declared itself a sovereign state, separating from the Federal Republic of Central America, which had been established after independence.

events.headline: First Constitution
events.text: Costa Rica adopted its first constitution, establishing the framework for its government and legal system, emphasizing democracy and civil rights.

events.headline: Filibuster War
events.text: Costa Rican forces, led by General Juan Rafael Mora Porras, successfully repelled the invasion of American filibuster William Walker, who aimed to establish a slave state.

events.headline: Coffee Export Boom
events.text: The coffee industry began to flourish, becoming a key driver of Costa Rica's economy and leading to increased exports and foreign investment.

events.headline: Abolition of the Army
events.text: Costa Rica abolished its army, redirecting military funds towards education and healthcare, which laid the foundation for its modern welfare state.

events.headline: New Constitution
events.text: A new constitution was adopted, solidifying democratic governance and human rights protections, and establishing the framework for a stable political system.

events.headline: National Parks System Established
events.text: Costa Rica established its national parks system, recognizing the importance of conservation and biodiversity, which has become a model for ecotourism.

events.headline: Economic Crisis
events.text: Costa Rica faced a severe economic crisis characterized by high inflation and unemployment, prompting significant reforms and adjustments in economic policy.

events.headline: Democratic Elections
events.text: Costa Rica held democratic elections, marking a return to stable governance after a period of political turmoil and economic challenges.

events.headline: Free Trade Agreement with Mexico
events.text: Costa Rica signed a free trade agreement with Mexico, paving the way for increased trade and economic integration within the region.

events.headline: CAFTA-DR Agreement
events.text: Costa Rica ratified the Central America-Dominican Republic Free Trade Agreement (CAFTA-DR), further integrating its economy with the United States and Central America.

events.headline: Renewable Energy Milestone
events.text: Costa Rica achieved a significant milestone by running on 100% renewable energy for 299 days, showcasing its commitment to sustainability and environmental protection.

events.headline: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.text: Costa Rica, like the rest of the world, faced the challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic, implementing measures to protect public health while managing economic impacts.

events.headline: Presidential Elections
events.text: Costa Rica held presidential elections, reflecting its ongoing democratic processes and the public's engagement in shaping the country's future.
